title: SCIM: a PATCH that replaces only name.givenName / name.familyName leaves displayName and sys_user.name on the old name
body:
## Edition / version
ObjectOS Enterprise, framework pin `e24136c2` (`@better-auth/scim` 1.7.12). Local SCIM run for objectstack-ai/cloud#3667.

## Measured
1. A user whose display name is "Renamed InOkta" gets `PATCH /Users/{id}` with Entra's path-addressed shape: `[{"op":"Replace","path":"name.givenName","value":"Entra"},{"op":"Replace","path":"name.familyName","value":"Style"}]`. The answer is 200, but:
   - `name.givenName` / `familyName` change;
   - `displayName`, `name.formatted` and **`sys_user.name` (what the console shows) keep "Renamed InOkta"**.
2. Okta's path-less replace (`{"op":"replace","value":{"name.givenName":…,"name.familyName":…}}`) behaves the same.
3. Only a PATCH of `displayName`, or a full PUT, moves `sys_user.name`.

The cause is vendor behaviour: `setNamePart` stores the part and never recomposes `formatted` / `displayName`. The code has a `composeName` helper, which only the `remove` path uses.

## Impact
Low while the IdP also sends `displayName`, as Entra's default mapping does when that attribute changes. A tenant whose mapping sends only given/family name keeps showing the old name in ObjectOS indefinitely.

## Expected
When `displayName` / `formatted` were derived from the parts (the same test `setFormattedName` already makes), recompose them after a part changes. Either upstream it to `@better-auth/scim`, or apply it in the host's `identity.reconcileUser` before the user row is written.
